patterns_data.top_pattern: CT PPO acute hospital spend surge in PA-required admissions
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual PPO acute hospital inpatient spend in CT
key_driver_codes: Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC
Chemotherapy without Acute Leukemia as Secondary Diagnosis with CC
patterns_data.pattern_details: CT PPO acute hospitals show the single largest increase, driven by both more inpatient use and higher paid amounts per admission in PA-required claims. The increase is concentrated in high-acuity inpatient care, especially craniotomy and chemotherapy episodes. This is a true operating pattern, not just a rate change or a pure volume spike.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is the largest identifiable spend driver and needs coordinated UM and reimbursement action in one market.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch a joint CT PPO inpatient action plan covering admission management, level-of-care review, and contract review for high-acuity acute hospital cases, starting with craniotomy and chemotherapy episodes.
evidence_summary: CT PPO acute hospitals added about $42.0M.
Admissions increased by 682 and claims by 337, while paid per admit increased by about $3.4K.
Craniotomy and endovascular intracranial cases added about $1.5M on 14 more admissions with roughly $19.0K higher paid per admit.
Chemotherapy cases added about $0.3M on 4 more admissions with roughly $13.5K higher paid per admit.

patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual HMO inpatient hospital spend in NY
patterns_data.pattern_details: NY inpatient growth is primarily being driven by more admissions rather than higher cost per admission. The main pressure sits in PA-required HMO acute hospital claims, with only a small additional FFS pocket. This points to a utilization management issue more than a reimbursement issue.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: When admissions rise while paid per admit falls, the biggest savings lever is reducing avoidable inpatient use rather than chasing rate changes.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a NY HMO admission management review focused on the added inpatient volume, including PA criteria, avoidable admits, and inpatient-to-outpatient opportunities.
evidence_summary: NY HMO acute hospitals added about $17.3M.
Admissions increased by 464 and claims by 245, while paid per admit decreased by about $21.0K.
A smaller NY FFS acute hospital pocket added about $75K.

patterns_data.top_pattern: A small set of hospitals is driving acute inpatient growth across several states and products
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual acute hospital inpatient spend in TX, WI, GA, CA and other states
key_driver_codes: Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC
Major Small and Large Bowel Procedures without CC/MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: Outside the two largest state spikes, inpatient spend is concentrating in a relatively small set of hospitals across HMO, POS, EPO, and some PPO business. The pattern mixes volume growth with higher paid amounts per admission and repeatedly shows up in high-acuity neuro, bowel, and uterine cases. This is a provider concentration story with network and steerage implications, not a uniform statewide trend.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Concentrated growth at a few hospitals creates targeted contracting, steerage, and case-management opportunities.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Build a provider action list for the named hospitals and review contract terms, referral patterns, and case management rules by product, starting with Medical City Plano, Aurora Medical Center - Sheboygan County, Baylor University Medical Center, and Emory Hospital Warner Robins.
evidence_summary: Across CA, FL, IN, KY, ME, NY, OH, TX, VA, and WI, HMO acute hospitals added about $8.6M, with Medical City Plano contributing about $1.7M and Aurora Medical Center - Sheboygan County about $0.9M.
TX Baylor University Medical Center added about $1.1M from volume growth on 64 more admissions.
GA HMO acute hospitals added about $2.5M, led by craniotomy at about $1.6M and bowel procedures at about $0.7M.
Additional emerging acute hospital pockets added about $3.8M across CA EPO, TX POS, MO EPO, IN POS, and smaller PPO and HMO segments.

patterns_data.top_pattern: CO has a concentrated neurosurgical and neuro-oncology inpatient pattern
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual HMO acute hospital neuro cases in CO
key_driver_codes: Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: CO shows a tightly concentrated neuro pattern centered on craniotomy and related brain diagnoses. Operationally, the state has both more admissions and sharply higher paid amounts in HMO acute hospitals, and clinically the same area is reinforced by brain neoplasm, aneurysm, and traumatic bleed cases. This should be treated as a focused high-acuity case-mix issue in one state rather than a broad inpatient trend.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A concentrated high-acuity neuro pattern can materially move spend and calls for case-level clinical and reimbursement review.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Perform a CO case-level review of craniotomy and related brain diagnoses to confirm severity, referral patterns, level of care, and contract performance at acute hospitals.
evidence_summary: CO HMO acute hospitals added about $3.4M, with craniotomy and endovascular intracranial cases contributing about $1.9M on 26 more admissions and roughly $73.7K higher paid per admit.
CO focused neuro case mix added about $4.2M from benign meningeal neoplasm, brain metastasis, and cranial nerve tumor diagnoses.
CO rare neuro outliers added about $3.0M, including cerebral aneurysm at about $1.1M and traumatic subdural hematoma at about $1.0M.
Additional CO neuro diagnoses added about $1.4M from frontal lobe malignancy and subdural hemorrhage cases.

patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Authorization classification and facility mapping affecting inpatient spend attribution
key_driver_codes: Chemotherapy without Acute Leukemia as Secondary Diagnosis with CC
patterns_data.pattern_details: Several findings point to spend moving between authorization or facility buckets rather than only reflecting true operating change. The largest issues are auth code distribution shifts and claims landing in Not Mapped facility categories. These should be treated as gating data and classification fixes before tightening UM rules or escalating provider actions.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If the underlying auth or facility mapping is wrong, business actions aimed at utilization or reimbursement can be misdirected.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Reconcile authorization coding and facility attribution for CA, WI, NY, CT, and IN, then rerun the impacted views before making UM or network changes.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Multiple groups are explicitly flagged for auth or mapping shifts and require validation before business action, including AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION and Not Mapped facility buckets.
evidence_summary: An unattributed auth code distribution shift tied to CA contributed about $5.0M.
WI auth code distribution shifts added about $1.7M, including about $1.2M in chemotherapy and about $0.4M tied to Aurora Medical Center - Sheboygan County.
NY HMO claims in the Not Mapped facility bucket added about $1.1M on 40 more admissions.
CT and CA Not Mapped facility buckets added about $0.9M combined, with a smaller IN pocket adding about $37K.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Post-acute and specialty facility use is creating site-of-care pressure
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual spend in Physical Rehab, long-term care, children's, and specialty inpatient settings
key_driver_codes: Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with CC
patterns_data.pattern_details: Spend growth is not limited to acute hospitals; it is also appearing in rehab, long-term care, children's, and other specialty settings. Much of this pressure is tied to orthopedic aftercare and similar follow-on care, suggesting a site-of-care or discharge-pathway issue. The pattern is smaller than the acute hospital spikes but has clear UM and steerage levers.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Site-of-care drift can raise total episode cost even when the originating inpatient event is unchanged.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Review discharge planning, prior authorization rules, and contract terms for rehab and specialty facility use, and redirect eligible cases to lower-cost settings where clinically appropriate.
evidence_summary: HMO Physical Rehab across CA, CO, IN, KY, NY, and VA added about $0.9M, led by NY at about $0.5M with roughly $39.5K higher paid per admit.
CA EPO Physical Rehab added about $0.5M on 10 more admissions with roughly $50.3K higher paid per admit.
Orthopedic aftercare case-mix in CA added about $1.3M across two focused clinical patterns.
Other site pockets included CT PPO long-term care hospital at about $0.1M, CA EPO children's at about $0.2M, and TX rehab across HMO and POS at about $0.4M combined.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Inpatient chemotherapy is emerging as a focused oncology cost driver
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Commercial Individual inpatient chemotherapy episodes in WI and CA
key_driver_codes: Chemotherapy without Acute Leukemia as Secondary Diagnosis with CC
patterns_data.pattern_details: The oncology signal is concentrated in inpatient chemotherapy rather than a broad cancer trend. WI is the main driver, and a smaller CA EPO acute hospital pocket reinforces the pattern. Because the action differs from other inpatient categories, this should be handled as a dedicated oncology site-of-care and appropriateness review.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Inpatient chemotherapy often has different utilization and site-of-care options than other medical-surgical admissions.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Review inpatient chemotherapy episodes for site-of-care appropriateness and pathway adherence, and shift eligible treatment to outpatient oncology settings where possible.
evidence_summary: WI inpatient chemotherapy added about $1.6M on 52 more admissions with roughly $10.5K higher paid per admit.
CA EPO acute hospital chemotherapy added about $0.3M on 2 more admissions with roughly $28.4K higher paid per admit.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Rare catastrophic cases are creating high-cost outlier pressure
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Low-frequency, high-cost inpatient outlier cases across TX, NY, GA, CA, OH, WI, and UNATTRIBUTED segments
key_driver_codes: Liver Transplant with MCC or Intestinal Transplant
ECMO or Tracheostomy with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours or Principal Diagnosis Except Face, Mouth and Neck with Major O.R. Procedures
patterns_data.pattern_details: This pattern is driven by a small number of very expensive catastrophic admissions, including transplant, ECMO or tracheostomy, severe sepsis, burns, and other major high-acuity cases. These cases are spread across several states, with a particularly visible TX provider concentration at Medical City Plano. The right response is case-level outlier management, not broad policy changes.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A few catastrophic cases can materially affect trend and require different handling than recurring utilization or reimbursement issues.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Stand up a case-level catastrophic outlier review covering transplant, ECMO or tracheostomy, severe sepsis, and similar episodes, including benefit eligibility, stop-loss exposure, and provider payment review.
patterns_data.validation_reason: These findings are flagged as low baseline and small volume, so case-level validation is needed before generalizing to broader policy changes.
evidence_summary: Rare high-cost cases across CA, OH, TX, UNATTRIBUTED, and WI added about $3.1M, including a NY liver transplant case at about $1.6M on 2 admissions.
TX ECMO or tracheostomy cases at Medical City Plano added about $1.4M across 8 admissions, with individual diagnoses contributing about $0.2M to $0.5M each.
GA rare high-cost cases added about $1.3M, including rectal cancer bowel surgery at about $0.4M and volvulus at about $0.3M.
